Sentence: "I think his views on (U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert) Rubin's comments were indeed what he himself thinks about the dollar," said Hank Note, chief dealer at Sumitomo Bank. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: Asked about Rubin's comment that a strong dollar was in U.S. interests, Sakakibara said the remark does not necessarily mean the United States supports a stronger dollar. Entities in the following order, first to last:
Sentence: "It's a strong dollar, not stronger. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: "It shows that Sakakibara is not for a stronger dollar either," said Sumitomo's Note. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: He had said then that the market's view on Japan's economy was too pessimistic and that he believed it was stronger than the market thought. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: A Lebanese military court on Friday sentenced to death in absentia the commander of Israel's surrogate militia in south Lebanon on treason charges. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: The court convicted General Antoine Lahd, head of the South Lebanon Army (SLA), of collaborating with Israel with which Lebanon is officially at war. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: Lahd, a 69-year-old former Lebanese army major-general, heads the 3,000-strong SLA militia which helps Israel hold a border zone in south Lebanon to ward off cross-frontier guerrilla raids on northern Israel. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: Lahd said a few days after the trial began on February 16 that Lebanese authorities must drop the charges or risk blocking any peace deal with the Jewish state. Entities in the following order, first to last:
Sentence: He said Israel was capable of pressuring Lebanon's Syrian-backed government to stop the legal pursuit. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: The charges against Lahd were: forming a hostile army, carrying weapons on Israel's side, helping Israel strip off a part of Lebanese territory by violence, forming an armed gang, killing or trying to kill Lebanese civilians by artillery shelling and kidnapping Lebanese citizens for long periods. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: Shortly before Lahd's trial began, a Beirut military prosecutor charged another 89 former Lebanese army soldiers with collaborating with Israel. Entities in the following order, first to last:
Sentence: No date has been set for the trial of the men, all members of the SLA living in the Israeli-held zone in south Lebanon. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: Israel and Lahd have repeatedly demanded safety guarantees for the SLA -- a mixed Christian-Shi'ite Moslem force -- which the Jewish states regards as loyal allies. Entities in the following order, first to last:
Sentence: Israel has said the Lebanese army must incorporate the SLA fighters into its ranks as an army brigade as a condition for peace. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: But Lebanese political analysts have said that would be out of the question and Lebanese authorities pre-empted the issue by taking legal action against Lahd. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: Former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres, calling Lahd "a great Lebanese patriot", said earlier this year Lebanon had insulted the SLA commander by ordering his arrest on the treason charges. Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: Peres, who was ousted in May by rightwing Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu, said there could not be real negotiations with Lebanon "unless it will stop the maltreatment of the SLA and its commanders." Entities in the following order, first to last:

Sentence: The Beirut military court also sentenced to life in jail in absentia Etian Saqr, former head of the pro-Israeli Guardians of the Cedars, a small rightwing Christian civil war militia. Entities in the following order, first to last:
